title: Duplicate faces created during marching cubes
abstract: ### Description: When running Marching Cubes on integer data, it can happen that it creates duplicated faces. In this case it happens specifically if I get 2 instances of case 7.4.2 (numbering as in [Lewiner _et al._ 2003](https://doi.org/10.1080/10867651.2003.10487582)) next to each other. In this minimal example I use `level = 0` for a `volume` in a shape of 3x2x2 `[[[13,-1],[-1,-7]],[[-1,1],[7,-7]],[[15,-9],[-3,-1]]]` When running the Marching Cubes algorithm I now get as output a mesh containing 18 triangles, 4 of which are overlapping. Specifically, faces 5 and 14 share the same set of 3 vertices and similarly faces 6 and 15 share the same set of 3 vertices. I think these faces should not exist in the final generated mesh; it makes no sense to me to have two parts of the isosurface right on top of each other. I think this is related to the fact that the face ambiguity test of the middle face in my volume amounts to 7*1-(-7)*(-1) = 0. Apparently the face test then somewhat arbitrarily evaluates as `positive` in both cases, creating these duplicated faces. ### Way to reproduce: ```python import numpy as np import skimage as ski mydata = np.array([[[13,-1],[-1,-7]],[ [-1,1],[7,-7]],[ [15,-9],[-3,-1]]], dtype=int) detailmesh = ski.measure.marching_cubes(mydata, level=0) print(detailmesh[1]) ``` yields as output ```python [[ 2 1 0] [ 1 2 3] [ 4 3 2] [ 5 4 2] [ 4 5 6] [ 7 6 5] [ 6 7 8] [ 0 8 7] [ 2 0 7] [11 10 9] [12 9 10] [ 9 12 13] [ 9 13 5] [ 6 5 13] [ 5 6 7] [ 8 7 6] [ 7 8 11] [ 7 11 9]] ``` Note that items 5 and 6 use the same vertices as items 14 and 15 ### Version information: ```Shell 3.13.2 | packaged by Anaconda, Inc. | (main, Feb 6 2025, 18:49:14) [MSC v.1929 64 bit (AMD64)] Windows-11-10.0.26200-SP0 scikit-image version: 0.25.0 numpy version: 2.2.5 ```
